prompt: Joost, the pricing lead, meets the legal team on Thursday about Voltmarkt's 2025 promotions and asks whether any of them took its discount off a list price that had just been raised. Take every promotion with a start_date from 1 January to 31 December 2025, both days included, and each of its products in promotion_products. For each product, use its price version in effect on the promotion's start_date: the version whose valid_from is on or before that day and whose valid_to is on or after it or missing (a missing valid_to means the price still holds). Compare that version's list_price_eur with the list_price_eur of the same product's version just before it; within a product, versions follow each other by valid_from. The product counts as raised when the price went up and that version took effect 0 to 14 days before the start_date (start_date minus valid_from is from 0 to 14), and as cut when the price went down in those same days. A version with no version before it is neither raised nor cut. Return one row for each promotion, with six columns in this order: promo_code; start_date; n_products, its number of products; n_raised; n_cut; and max_rise_pct, the largest rise among its raised products, as 100 times the new list price minus the old one, divided by the old one, rounded to 1 decimal, and missing when no product of the promotion was raised. Sort by n_raised from high to low, then by promo_code from A to Z.
hints: Next, give every price version the list price of the same product's version just before it.
Then match each 2025 promotion's products to the version in effect on its start_date, and count per promotion the products raised or cut 0 to 14 days before it began.
why_this_works: Taking the previous price product by product, then the version in effect on the start_date, compares the price the discount was taken from with the price just before it.
